I'll start with the mower. I can't recommend this mower enough! I wish I could give it more than 5 stars. I have 2 acres that have grown waist high over the fall and this spring I decided to tackle it with the Wild Badger after watching a few YouTube influencers who encouraged me. This little mower is a beast. It has started right up for me every time in the 6 weeks I have put it through h*ll. 

There's a second speed that kicks in if you push fast or through high grass. It has had no problem going through very tall and thick grass. The bagger is nice because I can feed all of this to my chickens. But for my needs, the bagger is a bit small because I have to stop often to empty it. For a normal sized lawn this should not be a big problem. There is also a mulching insert I use when I don't feel like emptying the bag.

I bought a second battery, and I recommend doing that if you plan to mow longer than about 40 minutes, which is what my batteries have lasted on average. Mowing on rough terrain, I'm ready for a break after 40 minutes, so this works out well for me. I haven't needed to tap into the second battery yet, but I'm glad I have it in case I need to do a lot of mowing at once.

I also bought the 3 year warranty on this because I doubted it would last. I'm glad I have that as well. 

The mower is mostly made from hard plastic, and that feels a bit flimsy, but so far I have not run into any problems. I have very difficult terrain on my acreage and although I have to raise the blades to accommodate mole hills and high areas, it has performed wonderfully. I get the feeling if you were rough with the mower, the wheels might crack off, but if you're careful and use it as it should, I think it will last. Again, having that warranty will give you some peace of mind.

I highly recommend this very affordable and very powerful battery powered mower.

As far as Lowes, I will never buy from them online again. I got a 2 in the morning text message telling me my item was shipping. Followed by numerous middle of the night texts that I did not appreciate one bit. When I contacted Lowes about this, they didn't seem to care at all. Why I Tried This Mower
I wanted to see if the Wild Badger Power 40 Volt Self-Propelled Lawn Mower could handle my 1/2-acre lot during the fall. Between grass clippings and leaves, I needed something quiet and cordless to make the job easier.

My Experience
Putting the mower together was quick and easy—no hassles there. It’s lightweight and really easy to move around, but I did notice the plastic wheels slipping on slight inclines, which got annoying. When I used the bagging option, the bag only filled to about 75% before I had to stop and empty it, which slowed things down. Plus, the batteries ran out before I could finish the job, and recharging them took longer than I expected.

When I switched to mulching, things went way smoother. It handled the mix of grass and leaves well, and I was able to finish the whole yard with both batteries.

What It Did for Me
The mower was super quiet, which was great—I didn’t feel like I was disturbing anyone. Mulching saved me time since I didn’t have to keep stopping to empty the bag. On the downside, the battery life isn’t quite enough for my yard when bagging, and the long charging time was frustrating.

My Take
This mower is a good fit for smaller, flat yards. It’s easy to use, does a great job mulching, and is lightweight. But for larger yards or places with inclines, the battery life, recharge time, and wheel traction might be a problem.

Overall, it’s a nice eco-friendly option, but it comes with a few trade-offs if you’ve got a bigger yard like mine.

It was nicely packaged.  After I removed everything from the box (see photo).
   I read the instruction manual to get an idea how to assemble the mower.  The manual failed that function badly.  It was obvious that the 2 large knobs were to be used to attach the lower handles to the mower deck (number 9 on page 6 of the manual).  After looking closely at the plastic ends of the lower handles I found one marked with an ‘L’ and one with an ‘R’ which I presumed indicated LEFT and RIGHT.  There were 2 shoulder screws which I guessed would be used to attach the upper handle to the lower handles.  That was easy even if not noted in the manual as there were no other screws in the supplied hardware.  Two plastic quick release knobs (number 5 on page 6 of the manual) with threaded inserts which I guessed were to go on the shoulder screws.  Then the question, do they go on the inside or outside of the handles?  The picture on the box indicated the quick release knobs must be on the outside of the handles.  I also found 2 fender washers and the mystery was, where do these go?  There was no mention of them in the manual.   I found a YOUTUBE video where I watched someone assemble a Wild Badger mower on top of a work bench.  When he finished, there were 2 washers left on the work bench top.  I guess he didn’t know where to put them either.  I did find another video of a young lady assembling the same mower as mine and she used the washers under the handle quick release knobs.  That made sense to me, so I used them there.  Note: the shoulder screws and washers are not shown anywhere in the User’s Manual.  So, with the handle installed, installation was completed.  I did find spelling errors in the manual.  It would have been easier if the authors of the manual had showed me a parts breakdown and told me nothing other than, “put it together”.
  Nothing left to do except charge the batteries and install them in the mower.  Even for dummies like me, it’s almost impossible to do this wrong.
  Now for the good stuff.  Except for the handles and blade the rest of the mower is basically plastic.  I think this is great because plastic doesn’t rust.  I store my mowers in a shed.  It’s easy to wash down with a hose after I finish mowing.  It’s probably a good idea to remove the batteries before the washdown.
  My intention for this mower is to use it to trim and get into tight spaces.  The mower will work for small to medium yard mowing with no problems.  It is light (less than 40 lbs. with the batteries installed.) and can be easily picked up, if need be.  On flat ground it rolls with no effort and you almost forget you’re pushing anything. 
  The one weak point with any electric mower is the batteries.  I was concerned about the run time.  The first time I used it for leaf collection and some weed and grass mowing.  It was used for 1.5 hours.  Yes, I timed it.  I checked the charge indicators on the batteries, and it indicated they still had HALF charge left in both batteries.  That was amazing.  I know there are things to consider, such as how tough the grass is to cut which may cause the motor to draw more current and the batteries will have a greater demand for power which will reduce the run 
 Time.
  So, my overall impression of this product is after its first use.  It exceeded my expectations.  I think it is a good value for the intended use.  Yes, I would recommend it without reservations even with my complaints about the manual.  I only gave it 4 stars due to the manual.

Results.ReviewText:
I couldn’t be happier with the Wild Badger Power 40 Volt 18-Inch Lawn Mower! This mower strikes the perfect balance between power, convenience, and eco-friendliness. Its 40-volt battery provides impressive power and a long runtime, allowing me to mow my entire yard on a single charge. Plus, the battery charges quickly, which is a huge bonus if I need to tackle additional tasks.

The 18-inch cutting deck is ideal for maneuvering in tight spaces while still covering enough ground to make mowing efficient. I love the fact that it’s lightweight and easy to push, making it a breeze to handle—even on uneven terrain. The height adjustment feature is another standout, as it lets me customize the cut for different areas of my lawn.

What really sets this mower apart is its quiet operation. I can mow early in the morning without disturbing the neighbors, and it’s so much more peaceful than using a gas-powered mower. The maintenance-free design is also a major plus—no more oil changes or dealing with fumes!

Overall, the Wild Badger Power 40 Volt 18-Inch Lawn Mower is an excellent choice for anyone looking for a reliable, efficient, and environmentally friendly way to keep their lawn looking great. Highly recommend!

Results.ReviewText:
Setup was a little difficult.  There weren’t many parts, but assembly of the handle took way longer than it should have because they don’t show a picture of the parts and where they all go.  All drawing show a straight handle bar, but the actual bars are angled, and there were no instructions on how to orient them.  After 10 minutes of head-scratching I determined that they will only go on one way, and there is a little raised plastic bump that must be aligned with another little plastic bump (see photo).  It turns out that the bar should be angled toward the ground.  

There are also 2 “levers” which are not even mentioned, and no guidance is provided on how to install them.  After another 10 minutes of head-scratching I determined that they are used to keep pressure on the bar connection.  It’s a little disappointing that they are made of plastic; I don’t expect them to last long.  

The mower mulches pretty well, but the mulching insert attaches using two holes and a slot get clogged with grass clippings after mowing with the bag attached.  The blade is a thin 1/16 inch thick, so I don’t think it would last very long hitting rocks and other debris.

The bag is pretty small and filled up after only 2 minutes of cutting high grass.  It has a little flap which flips up as you mow and does not flip up once the bag is not full – it actually works pretty well.  The bag is a little difficult to empty since there is no way to widen the opening to dump it; you can only dump it through the intake shoot.

The mower is super light and I could easily lift it into my car for transportation.  The right side has a one-handed cutting height adjustment which works well, and the automatic “Turbo” mode for thick grass performed admirably.  The mower did bog down and turn off on the lowest cut setting (#1), but at that point it was cutting the grass bald.  On a more realistic setting (#2), the mover did well, even in thick grass and with the mulching insert.

OVERALL, if you have a small yard (1/4 to 1/3 acre) that is fairly well maintained and level, I think this mover would do well.  However, if your yard is larger, or bumpy and rocky, then I would not recommend this mower.
Results.Title: Nice little mower

Results.ReviewText: I was really hoping this would tackle my yard as it's less than 1/4 acre but unfortunately this little mower did not make the cut (see what I did there). OK, the good bits - Everything is nicely packed and assembles very easily. The battery charged up without issue and the mower started and operated as it should. The entire mower is lightweight and simple to operate. Now the not so good - This model is not self drive and even with its light weight the thick St Augustine grass just grabbed on and made the mow difficult. The battery is 40v at 4Ah and even for my small yard a single charge was not enough to cut the entire lawn. Build quality is very questionable and I do not see this mower lasting through a season. If you are going to make the switch to electric you may want to go for a more robust and tested product.
